record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: Does the reverse-mathematical strength of either the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem or Milliken theorem depend on the splitting properties of the trees, such as whether the trees are two-branching, three-branching, or finitely but unboundedly branching?

evidence.quote: Does the strength of either the Halpern-Läuchli Theorem or the Milliken Theorem depend on the splitting properties of the trees?
are two-branching trees weaker than three-branching trees,..., weaker than finitely but unboundedly branching trees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For a tree T ⊆ ω^{<ω}, say T is k-branching if every node has exactly k immediate successors, and finitely branching if every node has finitely many immediate successors (with the number possibly varying from node to node and unbounded along T). For a finite sequence of trees (T_0,…,T_{d-1}), a "level product" is a set of the form ∏_{i<d} T_i(n) where T_i(n) denotes the n-th level of T_i.

Halpern–Läuchli Theorem (HL). For every d ≥ 1, every d-tuple of finitely-branching, perfect trees (T_0,…,T_{d-1}) without terminal nodes, and every finite coloring c : ⋃_n ∏_{i<d} T_i(n) → r, there exist strong subtrees S_i ⊆ T_i (i<d) with a common level set such that c is constant on ⋃_n ∏_{i<d} S_i(n).

Milliken's Tree Theorem (MTT). For every finitely-branching, perfect tree T without terminal nodes, every k ≥ 1, and every finite coloring of the set of strong subtrees of T of height k, there is a strong subtree S ⊆ T (of infinite height, with a common level set) such that all height-k strong subtrees of S receive the same color.

Both theorems can be restricted to the class of k-branching trees (for a fixed k ≥ 2) or to the class of finitely-but-unboundedly branching trees, yielding variants HL_k, MTT_k, HL_{fin}, MTT_{fin}.

Problem. Working in the framework of reverse mathematics over the base system RCA_0, determine whether the proof-theoretic strength of the Halpern–Läuchli Theorem or of Milliken's Tree Theorem depends on the splitting type of the trees involved. Specifically:

(a) For each fixed k ≥ 2, is HL_k strictly weaker (over RCA_0) than HL_{k+1}? Is HL_k strictly weaker than HL_{fin}? Are HL_2, HL_3, …, HL_{fin} all equivalent over RCA_0, or do they form a strict hierarchy?

(b) The analogous question for MTT_k versus MTT_{k+1} and MTT_{fin}.

Resolve these comparisons by either exhibiting equivalences over RCA_0 (or a suitable conservative extension) or by separating the principles via ω-models.
artifact.category_tag: Reverse mathematics of Ramsey-type tree theorems
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (notably Anglès d'Auriac–Cholak–Dzhafarov–Monin–Patey, "Milliken's tree theorem and its applications: a computability-theoretic perspective", arXiv:2007.09739) gives a complete reverse-mathematics classification of Milliken's tree theorem for finitely-branching trees, establishing equivalences (including via ACA_0-type principles) that are uniform in the branching, and shows the Halpern–Läuchli theorem is computably true for finitely-branching trees. This indicates that for the standard formulations the strength does not increase with the branching, but the precise hierarchy as the branching varies (k vs. k+1 vs. unboundedly branching) was not fully delineated as posed; thus the question is partially answered.

status_evidence.title: Milliken's tree theorem and its applications: a computability-theoretic perspective
status_evidence.snippet: A careful analysis of the Halpern-Läuchli theorem shows that it can be carried out effectively... yielding a comprehensive classification of the computable content of Milliken's tree theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a complete reverse-mathematical classification of Milliken's theorem for finitely-branching trees, addressing the dependence on branching.

status_evidence.title: Milliken's tree theorem and its applications (Patey notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Reverse mathematics of Milliken's tree theorem and Halpern-Läuchli, including treatment of branching.
status_evidence.claim: Computability-theoretic strength of HL and MTT analyzed across branching types.
